# Agent Babysitter (abs)

> Agent Babysitter is an open-source remote control for Claude Code that lets
> developers monitor, message, start and resume AI coding sessions from Telegram.
> It watches a Claude Code session running on the developer's own machine, sends a
> written summary to their phone when a task finishes, and takes the reply straight
> back into that same live session. Screenshots the model reads directly, voice
> notes transcribed and spoken locally, and Claude usage limits all work from the
> chat. One bash script plus Anthropic's official Claude Code Telegram plugin — no
> server, no webhook, no open port, and no second copy of the session.

Shorter: control Claude Code from Telegram.

Install on macOS or Linux, with Claude Code already installed and logged in: pipe
https://agentbabysitter.com/install.sh into bash. The exact one-line command, and
the command for pinning any older version, is on the Releases page below.

- Current version: 3.7.2. First public release: July 2026. MIT licensed. Free.
- Source: https://github.com/Pranjalab/AgentBabysitter
- Built and maintained by one developer, Pranjal (https://github.com/Pranjalab).

## What it answers

- Getting a Telegram notification when a Claude Code task finishes.
- Replying from an iPhone or Android phone into the same live Claude Code session.
- Running Claude Code remotely over SSH or in tmux and following it from a phone.
- Monitoring a long-running or autonomous AI coding agent while away from the desk.
- Sending a screenshot or photo that Claude reads directly.
- Voice notes both ways, transcribed and spoken on the developer's own machine —
  no cloud speech vendor.
- Checking Claude usage limits without going back to the terminal.
- Keeping the bot private: PIN pairing, a terminal-set allowlist, destructive-command
  blocking for remote-driven turns, and control phrases sent as a whole message.
- Named personas — abs, ceo, cto, friend, or one you write — chosen at launch.
- Reading and editing every layer abs puts in front of Claude, including what it
  remembers, with `abs prompt`.

## Honest limits

- Telegram is not end-to-end encrypted, so Telegram's servers see the messages.
  Do not use it where that matters.
- Messages are read between turns: you can halt the plan and steer the next step,
  not interrupt the step already running.
- A sleeping laptop suspends the session and resumes it on wake; nothing is lost,
  but nothing progresses meanwhile. Uninterrupted work wants a machine that stays
  awake.
- Windows is untested; WSL should work.
- It is a side project, maintained by one person.
